protections: P1: a client-supplied executable field (autoEvalCodeOnHTML) must not be relayed by the socket server, or eval'd by clients, unless a trusted server-side sender produced it. Evidence: plugin/YPTSocket/script.js:567-568, plugin/YPTSocket/Message.php:228-244
P2: the relayed 'callback' value must be a plain JS identifier before it is concatenated into eval'd code. Evidence: plugin/YPTSocket/script.js:91-95, plugin/YPTSocket/Message.php:297-298

P3 (A's guard): the sender display identity shown in the call toast must come from the token or be escaped, not from fields the caller supplies. Evidence: plugin/YPTSocket/Message.php:230-235, plugin/WebRTC/call/caller.js:90

masking: T6 only matters once T5 is fixed server-side: a top-level callback check in msgToResourceId leaves the nested recursion at script.js:47-49 open.
T3 only matters once T1/T2 are fixed by stripping the 'msg' sub-key.

conflicts.what: The natural client-side fix (remove or ignore the eval at script.js:567-568) also breaks LiveLinks removal (LiveLinks.php:410), because no socketRemoveLiveLinks JS function exists. The server-side fix must keep the field for sentFrom==='php' tokens (functions.php:9, YPTSocket.php:327) and must not trust the caller-supplied isCommandLine (YPTSocket.php:324).

Validating callback against a strict identifier allowlist is safe for every in-repo callback name found (e.g. LiveLinks.php:411 'socketRemoveLiveLinks', WebRTC/call/caller.js:50 'incomeCall'). Rejecting the whole frame instead of only blanking callback would also drop legitimate autoEvalCodeOnHTML frames.

fairness_risks: Server-sent autoEvalCodeOnHTML (LiveLinks.php:410) must keep being evaluated. A rule of 'never eval socket code' contradicts it unless the test allows server-only provenance.

Users must keep messaging each other directly (to_users_id and resourceId targeting at Message.php:238-241; calls at WebRTC/call/caller.js:50). A rule that blocks browser-originated relay entirely would break calls.
Legitimate frames carry the payload in both 'msg' (a JSON string) and 'json' (an object) (YPTSocket.php:323-325). A filter that rejects string msg or the json key would break server sends.

If tests do not pin the provenance discriminator, a solver who removes the client eval and a solver who strips server-side (both servers) would both be correct; tests must target behaviour, not the fix site.

design.why: T1 is the advisory route (easy anchor). T2 is the default second server class with a strong 'variant' dismissal (deepseek-type). T4 is the must-keep LiveLinks eval plus the sentFrom-vs-isCommandLine discriminator (mimo-type coupled value). It also makes T2 independent of T1: once the client eval must keep working, the fix has to be server-side in both Message.php and MessageSQLiteV2.php, so there are 4 groups instead of 3. T5 is the callback eval, which has no protection and a 'not in the report' dismissal (xhard for DeepSeek). T7 is a wrong-object identity check left by A's from_identification-only fix, in another plugin. These are four independent fix sites with different reasons to dismiss. Without a T4 must-keep test, a single client-side change closes T1-T3, and the stack falls to 3 groups.
